operationName: Ebola PHEIC Response — 2026 Bundibugyo Outbreak, DRC & Uganda
heroHeadline: Suspected Cases Pass 1,000 — Confirmed Cases Nearly Double as WHO DG Visits DRC
heroSubtitle: By 31 May 2026, the 2026 DRC-Uganda Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak had surpassed 1,077 suspected cases and 246 probable deaths — breaching the 1,000-case threshold just 14 days after the WHO PHEIC declaration. DRC lab-confirmed cases surged from 125 (May 29) to approximately 225 (May 30), nearly doubling in 48 hours as expanded BSL-3 mobile labs in Ituri accelerated diagnostic throughput; Uganda updated its confirmed count to 9. WHO Director-General Tedros visited Bunia on 30 May, issuing a 'maximum mobilization' emergency appeal on 31 May calling for the $153M gap in WHO's Emergency Contingency Fund to be filled and an accelerated ChAdOx1 BDBV clinical trial framework to be finalized within 21 days. Uganda's 4-week DRC border closure entered its fourth day. The Mongbwalu cluster — where 25+ patients escaped attacked ETUs in May 23–26 incidents — remains a critical uncaptured transmission nucleus with DRC contact tracing coverage still below 50%.
footerNote: Data sourced from WHO Situation Reports, CDC Ebola Situation Summary, DRC Ministry of Health (MSANTE), Uganda Ministry of Health, ECDC, MSF field reports, Al Jazeera, CGTN, Oxford University Jenner Institute, CEPI, and ReliefWeb. Case counts and CFR figures are rapidly evolving.
